title: Sell Mineral Rights in Moundville, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Moundville, AL | Tuscaloosa County
metaDescription: Hold mineral rights near Moundville, AL, south Tuscaloosa County? Get an honest, title-checked offer before you sign anything with a landman.
heroLead: Moundville sits near the southern edge of the Black Warrior coal basin, where the Pottsville coal measures that fuel coalbed methane wells farther north begin giving way to the Cretaceous chalk of Alabama's Black Belt.
intro: Moundville is better known for the archaeological site than for oil and gas, but the ground south of Tuscaloosa along the Black Warrior River has still seen its share of mineral leasing over the decades — just at a lower density than the core CBM fields around Brookwood and Oak Grove to the north. That flank position matters for value: a Moundville-area interest is more likely to be undeveloped or lightly leased than one sitting inside an active coalbed methane unit, and pricing has to start from that reality rather than an assumption borrowed from farther up the basin.

sections.heading: Flank of the Basin, Not the Core
paragraphs: Being on the edge of the productive coal trend doesn't mean your minerals are worthless, but it does mean the honest starting point is different than for land sitting inside an active unit. We look at what's actually been leased or drilled near your specific tract in southern Tuscaloosa County before we say anything about value, rather than pricing off the more active fields to the north.

sections.heading: Old River-Bottom Land and Family Title
paragraphs: A lot of the acreage along the Black Warrior River near Moundville has stayed in the same families for generations, often passed down informally without much attention to what, exactly, was owned below the surface. Before we make an offer, we pull the Tuscaloosa County records to confirm whether your family's mineral estate was ever severed from the land and how it has moved through the generations since.

faqs.question: Has there ever been drilling near Moundville?
faqs.answer: Some, though at lower density than the core CBM fields north around Brookwood and Oak Grove. We check what's actually on record for your specific tract before we quote anything.

faqs.question: Our land has never been leased. Is there any point in talking to you?
faqs.answer: Yes — undeveloped acreage on the flank of an active basin still has value, it's just priced differently than a producing interest. Send us the legal description and we'll give you a straight read.

faqs.question: How do you confirm what we actually own?
faqs.answer: We pull the deed and probate records at the Tuscaloosa County Courthouse ourselves before we ever put a number in front of you.
